I am an old woman in Mtwara, and this small piece of land is what feeds my family. I have no money for chemical fertilizer or hybrid seeds from the shop — I keep my own maize seeds from last season like my mother taught me, and I put the goat droppings and kitchen ash on the field. I intercrop with cowpea and cassava so if the rains fail, something will still come. My children and grandchildren help me weed; I cannot afford to hire people.
